question: Not shared. P-845's 'aerobic exercise led to the most benefits' concerns cognition and independent living, in a narrative tally of RCTs in MCI and AD. P-848's resistance-first ranking concerns neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPI family) in older adults with MCI or dementia. Its resistance node rests on three dementia/AD trials, and only three of its 34 studies met Petersen MCI criteria. The outcome (cognition/function vs NPS) differs, and the population behind P-848's resistance estimate is dementia, not MCI. On the one outcome both address, cognition, P-848 finds no significant difference between exercise types. P-1131 is a context paper, not part of the pair.
metric: Mismatch. P-845 reports no metric of any kind (a narrative verdict; the article states that no data were used). P-848 reports SMDs against active control, with SUCRA ranks.

figures.P-845: No estimate and no interval: an ordinal verdict (aerobic best) from a table of 34 RCTs, with the qualitative statement that there is 'very little evidence that non-aerobic exercise provides these beneficial effects'. No interval can be derived, because no quantity is estimated.
figures.P-848: NPS: resistance exercise vs active control SMD -1.70 (95% CI -3.12 to -0.29), SUCRA 91.8%; multi-component -0.70 (-1.32 to -0.08); no other comparison significant; I2 = 93.2%. Cognition: multi-component ranks first (SUCRA 80.2%), with no statistically significant differences between exercise types.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure. P-845 gives no estimate on any outcome, so there is nothing to set against P-848's NPS SMD. On cognition, the outcome P-845's verdict mainly rests on, P-848 reports no significant difference between exercise types, which is consistent with, not contrary to, any aerobic-first reading. Neither paper reports aerobic against resistance exercise on NPS in MCI with aligned modality classes. The same trial is classed differently: Holthoff 2015 is 'Aerobic' in P-845 and 'Resistance exercise' in P-848.
reason: The two 'best modality' claims concern different outcomes (cognition and independent living for P-845, neuropsychiatric symptoms for P-848), and P-848's resistance estimate comes entirely from dementia trials (condition 1). P-845 computes no estimate at all, so there is no shared metric (condition 2) and no interval against which a difference beyond uncertainty could be shown (condition 4). On cognition, P-848 finds no significant difference between exercise types.

quotes.quote: We determined that aerobic exercise led to the most benefits, that many cognitive domains improve with exercise, and that aerobic exercise enhances the ability for independent living.
However, there is very little evidence that non-aerobic exercise provides these beneficial effects
No data was used for the research described in the article.

The NMA results revealed that resistance exercise (SMD = −1.70, 95 % CI: −3.12, −0.29) and multi-component exercise (SMD = −0.70, 95 % CI: −1.32, −0.08) significantly reduced NPS compared to the active control conditions.
The NMA results revealed that there were no statistically significant differences between exercise types (Fig. 3B).
3 explored the effects of resistance exercise (C´amara-Calmaestra et al., 2025; Fleiner et al., 2017; Holthoff et al., 2015)
Only three studies focused on the effects of exercise interventions on older adults meeting Petersen’s diagnostic criteria for MCI.
